To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of an urban CHP plant with a natural gas expansion plant, a heat pump in a public school and a public gas refueling station, is a viable solution to reduce the energy consumption of the school and the energy costs of the refueling station, while at the same time reducing the CO2 emissions of the school and of the refueling system, and the CO emissions of the refueling stations.
The energy saving of the proposed system is about 20% compared to the current situation, and the CO2 emissions are reduced by about 20% as well.
the integration of CHP and TE units in an urban area allows for a significant energy and environmental benefit.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a detailed simulation of the energy flows of the integrated system, with the aim of optimizing the energy production and consumption, as well as the heat and cold distribution, and to evaluate the economic feasibility of the system.
the design, simulation and control of the integrated system, which will be implemented in a real demonstrator, and with the evaluation of the energy and environmental benefits.
the design of a control strategy to manage the energy flows between the different users of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the integration of the TE in the expansion station, together with the use of the EP surplus for the school and the RS, and the heat recovery for the DHN, is a very promising solution for a sustainable energy management.
the integrated system will provide a reduction of the energy consumption of the school and RS of about 30%, and a reduction of CO2 emissions of 30% and 40%, respectively.

the integrated system will be capable to reduce the primary energy consumption of the whole system by about 10%, while reducing the greenhouse gas emissions by about 15% and saving about 1 million euros per year.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy saving and the reduction of CO2 emissions will be obtained by the combined production and conversion of energy in an urban integrated system, which includes a CHP unit and a turbo-expander.

the integration of the CHP system and the TE system in the gas distribution network, with the consequent recovery of mechanical energy, is a valid alternative to the current practice of gas distribution.

the integration of the energy system in an urban area, by means of a combined heat and power system, can lead to a significant reduction of the primary energy consumption and of the environmental impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of CHP units with TE and DHN can be a viable option to increase the energy efficiency of a gas expansion station.
the use of CHPs and heat pumps in an integrated system can lead to an overall energy and environmental saving.

the use of a turboexpander in the natural gas expansion station can be an effective way to reduce energy consumption and emissions, and that this solution can be integrated in an energy efficient district heating and cooling system.
